notes.text:
An exact recognition bridge in the ENTIRE original class, with a constructive proof.

Retain K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8 and the supplied compact, good, strict, smooth, separated, boundaryless pure surface X=(Gm^2)^an/<(t,2),(3,t)>. Genuine nonalgebraization and coherent descent are NOT certified. Keep local rho=|r|^2/2, theta=DD rho and reference raw mass two. C is the ENTIRE minimal continuous CLD class of weights a with rho+a locally in the smallest continuous sheaf containing smooth positive-Hessian generators and closed under local uniform limits. G means precisely limits of ACTUAL continuous a_n in C decreasing everywhere, with inf E(a_n)>-infinity. E(a)=(1/3)int a(theta^2+theta_a theta+theta_a^2), theta_a=theta+DD a. No operator or limiting energy is assigned to an unrepresented function.

For bounded-above u:X->[-infinity,infinity), and ordinary real continuous h>u everywhere, define Gamma_u(h)=sup{E(a):a in ENTIRE C, u<=a<h everywhere}, with sup empty=-infinity, and A(u)=inf_{h continuous,h>u}Gamma_u(h). A(u) is an obstacle-feasibility profile, not a definition of extended energy E(u). A cozero set is {f>0} for continuous f:X->[0,1].

THEOREM. u belongs to the ORIGINAL G if and only if (i) every rational sublevel {u<q} is cozero, and (ii) A(u)>-infinity. This checks actual presentations; it is not a claim that these conditions hold for an unspecified target potential. For real continuous u the conditions are equivalent to u in ORIGINAL C. For every positive Radon mu of raw mass two with FULL D(mu)=sup_ENTIRE_C(E(a)-int a mu)<infinity, a recognized u has a finite moment and int u mu>=A(u)-D(mu). In particular a recognized potential cannot have a pole at a finite-FULL-D whole Dirac point.

Bounded structural reconstruction. Constant addition preserves the minimal sheaf: for fixed c, the continuous f for which f+c belongs to that sheaf form a uniformly closed sheaf containing its smooth positive-Hessian generators. Global uniform closure of C follows from its local definition. CLD recursive products of actual continuous psh potentials are positive closed; their dpsh multilinear extension and invariance under smooth DD-null changes glue B(a,b)=theta_a wedge theta_b globally. Locally a=(rho+a)-rho is dpsh. The defining derivative identity gives B(a,b)-theta^2=DD(a theta_b)+DD(b theta). The global constant test 1 has compact support on compact X and DD1=0. Evaluating these exact currents therefore proves that every bounded mixed mass is two. Positive top currents are Radon, so E is real on C. Since theta_(a+c)=theta_a, E(a+c)=E(a)+2c. This reconstruction uses no nonsmooth Green identity, energy concavity, or generated-operator theorem.

Barrier proof. If h_n are ordinary continuous and decrease to u, then {u<q}=union_n{h_n<q}. The uniformly convergent continuous series f_q=sum_n 2^-n min(1,(q-h_n)_+) is positive exactly there. Conversely choose an integer M>=sup u and v=exp(u-M), with exp(-infinity)=0. For each rational q<M choose continuous f_q in [0,1] positive exactly on {u<q}. Put r_q=exp(q-M) and k_(q,j)=r_q+(1-r_q)(1-j f_q)_+, j>=1. Each is continuous, positive and dominates v: on u>=q it is one; on u<q it is at least r_q>v. At a point with u<M, rational q>u can approach u (or tend to -infinity at a pole), and large j makes k_(q,j)=r_q. At u=M all these functions are one. Their pointwise infimum is therefore v. Enumerate the countable pairs (q,j), take K_n to be their first-n minimum, and set h_n=M+log K_n. These are REAL continuous functions decreasing to u at EVERY point, including poles. Open rational sublevels also prove upper semicontinuity. No countable dense set or metrizable carrier is assumed.

Recognition proof, necessity. An actual a_n decreasing to u with E(a_n)>=L supplies the cozero sublevels by the barrier proof. For fixed continuous h>u, the open sets {a_n<h} increase and cover compact X. A finite subcover gives a single global n with u<=a_n<h. Thus Gamma_u(h)>=L for every obstacle and A(u)>=L.

Recognition proof, sufficiency. Obtain ordinary continuous h_n decreasing to u from the cozero condition. Choose real L<A(u), epsilon_n=2^(-n-2), s_n=sum_(k>=n)epsilon_k=2^(-n-1). The obstacle H_1=h_1+epsilon_1 is strictly above u, so choose actual b_1 in C with u<=b_1<H_1 and E(b_1)>L. For n>=2 set H_n=min(h_n+epsilon_n,b_(n-1)+epsilon_(n-1)), an ordinary continuous obstacle strictly above u. Since Gamma_u(H_n)>=A(u)>L, choose actual b_n in C with u<=b_n<H_n and E(b_n)>L. Its minimum is NEVER declared psh. Set a_n=b_n+s_n. Then a_(n+1)<a_n because s_n=epsilon_n+s_(n+1); u<=a_n<h_n+epsilon_n+s_n; and E(a_n)=E(b_n)+2s_n>L. The upper error tends to zero, so these actual globally continuous original-C weights decrease everywhere to u, including at its poles. This proves the required G membership rather than declaring it.

Continuous corollary. Continuous u has the barrier u+1/n. If u is in C, this is already an actual finite-lower-energy presentation. Conversely an actual a_n decreasing to real continuous u converges uniformly: for every positive delta, the increasing open sets {a_n<u+delta} cover compact X and hence one of them is all of X. Local uniform closure therefore puts u in C. This argument uses actual continuous tails.

Moment proof. For every a admissible under h, FULL dual finiteness and positivity give E(a)<=D(mu)+int h mu. Hence Gamma_u(h)<=D(mu)+int h mu, also if its admissible set is empty. A constant obstacle bounds A(u) above by a finite number; recognition bounds it below. Ordinary barriers h_n decreasing to u give strict obstacles h_n+1/n and A(u)<=D(mu)+int h_n mu+2/n. Monotone convergence for h_1-h_n gives int h_n->int u, possibly initially -infinity. The real lower bound rules out -infinity and proves int u mu>=A(u)-D(mu). Constant translation gives Gamma_(u+c)(h+c)=Gamma_u(h)+2c and A(u+c)=A(u)+2c, preserving raw mass two.

notes.text:
An actual-carrier obstruction to every decreasing continuous presentation, hence the ENTIRE original G.

On exactly the surface and original class of OWN n1, let g be the image of the joint unit Gauss point of z1,z2. THEOREM: {g} is not a G_delta subset of the actual ordinary analytic topology of X. Therefore the bounded function u_g(g)=1, u_g(y)=0 for y!=g is upper semicontinuous and is outside every pointwise decreasing-sequence limit of ordinary real continuous functions. In particular it is outside the ENTIRE original G, irrespective of an energy lower bound. This is an obstruction to a proposed recognition shortcut; no psh status, finite energy, operator, or prescribed-equation nonexistence is assigned to this indicator.

Proof of the analytic assertion. On the torus let V={|r_i|<1/4}. The deck element (m,n) multiplies the coordinates by (t^m 3^n,2^m t^n), so shifts r by (m,n), because |2|=|3|=1 and |t|=exp(-1). Distinct translates of V are disjoint. The quotient topology identifies V homeomorphically with its ordinary open image. This supplies only the needed topological chart, not coherent descent or nonalgebraization.

Take any countable collection of open neighbourhoods of g and lift to V. The defining seminorm topology of affine torus analytification is the weakest topology making all evaluations |P|, P in K[z1^+/-1,z2^+/-1], continuous. Each neighbourhood therefore contains a basic neighbourhood specified by finitely many Laurent-polynomial norm constraints. Collect the countably many nonzero P_l involved. At g each has norm M_l equal to the maximum coefficient norm. Divide each P_l by a coefficient of norm M_l. Its coefficients are in the valuation ring and its reduction is a nonzero Laurent polynomial over the residue field C.

Let F be the subfield of C generated over Q by all coefficients of these reductions. It is countable, since finite rational expressions in a countable set form a countable set. The complex elements algebraic over a countable field form a countable set: there are countably many polynomials, with finitely many roots each. Choose alpha in C transcendental over F, then beta in C transcendental over the countable field F(alpha), using uncountability of C. Thus alpha,beta are nonzero and algebraically independent over F. Every nonzero reduced Laurent polynomial in the collected family is nonzero at (alpha,beta), as follows after multiplying by a monomial.

At the rigid point p=(alpha,beta), viewed as constants in K, both coordinates have norm one and every normalized polynomial evaluation has nonzero residue, hence norm one. Therefore |P_l(p)|=M_l=|P_l(g)| for ALL l. The rigid point belongs to V and all of the chosen basic neighbourhoods, and therefore all of the original countably many neighbourhoods. It is distinct from g because |z1-alpha|(p)=0 but |z1-alpha|(g)=1. Local injectivity preserves this distinction in X. This proves that no countable intersection of open neighbourhoods can isolate g.

Since X is Hausdorff, {g} is closed and the indicated singleton indicator is upper semicontinuous. If it had a decreasing ordinary continuous presentation, the cozero barrier lemma proved in OWN n1 would make {u_g<1/2}=X minus {g} a cozero set. Its complement would then be the zero set of a continuous nonnegative f, equal to the countable intersection of open sets {f<1/n}, contradicting the preceding paragraph. Thus NO original-C sequence presentation exists. The conclusion concerns the entire original G rather than any fan, pencil, radial, or finite-log-max subclass.
